title: U.S. House · Maine's 1st District
area: Southern Maine, including Portland, Biddeford, Sanford, and the southern coastal region.

context.text: Incumbent Chellie Pingree ran unopposed in the Democratic primary (Tiffany Roberts did not make the ballot). Ronald C. Russell won the Republican primary over Joshua Pietrowicz.

summary.text: Chellie Pingree is the Democratic incumbent for Maine's 1st District, which she has represented since 2009. Before Congress she ran a farm and a knitwear business on North Haven, served in the Maine Senate (including as majority leader), and led Common Cause. She sits on the House Appropriations and Agriculture committees.

background.text: Born April 2, 1955, in Minneapolis, Minnesota, the youngest of four children; moved to Maine as a teenager.
Attended the University of Southern Maine and earned a B.A. from the College of the Atlantic in 1979.

Moved to North Haven, Maine, where she and her husband ran a small farm, and in 1981 she started North Island Yarn (later North Island Designs), a knitting-kit business she sold in 1993; she also served on the school board and as town tax assessor.

Member of the Maine Senate from 1992 to 2000, representing Knox County; elected Senate majority leader by her peers in 1996. She sponsored the MaineRx prescription drug pricing bill in her last session.
Ran unsuccessfully against U.S. Sen. Susan Collins in 2002.
Served as national president and CEO of Common Cause from 2003 to 2007.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2008, the first woman elected to Congress from Maine's 1st District. She previously served on the Rules and Armed Services committees and currently sits on the Appropriations and Agriculture committees.

Received a 2017 James Beard Leadership Award for work on food system reform; her office says provisions of her agriculture legislation were included in the 2014 and 2018 Farm Bills. Co-owns Nebo Lodge, a bed and breakfast and restaurant on North Haven, started in 2006.

priorities.text: Says the U.S. must prevent global average temperatures from rising beyond 1.5 degrees Celsius and calls for economy-wide action to transition the energy system.
priorities.quote: If the United States doesn't take immediate, economy-wide action at all levels of government, our health and natural resources that support our economic growth could face irreparable harm. We must prevent average global temperatures from increasing beyond 1.5 degrees Celsius through economic incentives.

priorities.text: Says gun violence is preventable and calls on Congress to act, citing the October 2023 Lewiston mass shooting.
priorities.quote: Gun violence is preventable, and it's shameful that so many in Congress have blocked any legislation that would end this uniquely American epidemic.

priorities.text: Says both the Israeli and Palestinian people deserve to live in peace and lists actions she has taken toward a bilateral ceasefire, humanitarian aid delivery, and an end to the Gaza war.
priorities.quote: Both the Israeli people and the Palestinian people deserve to live in peace. I want my constituents to have a full understanding of all the actions I have taken to bring about a bilateral permanent ceasefire, swiftly deliver humanitarian aid, and bring an end to this war.

positions.summary: Describes herself as a longtime member of the Pro-Choice Caucus and lists bills she has cosponsored to protect abortion access, including the Women's Health Protection Act.
positions.quote: As a member of the Pro-Choice Caucus, I have been a longtime champion of reproductive freedom, and have cosponsored and helped pass several bills in the House to protect those freedoms

positions.summary: Voted for the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act and says she supported House-passed bills for enhanced background checks, a large-capacity magazine ban, and a federal red-flag law.
positions.quote: Though I support actions that go much further, I was proud to vote for this package that included funding for red flag laws, enhanced background checks for buyers under 21, investments in mental health, and more life-saving provisions.

positions.summary: Calls for immediate, economy-wide action to keep warming below 1.5 degrees Celsius and voted for the Inflation Reduction Act, describing it as the largest U.S. climate investment in history.
positions.quote: It is no exaggeration to say the Inflation Reduction Act is the most significant investment to fight climate change in U.S. history.

positions.summary: Says the Inflation Reduction Act makes large corporations and the wealthiest taxpayers pay their fair share through a 15% corporate minimum tax on billion-dollar-profit corporations and stronger IRS enforcement against wealthy tax cheats.
positions.quote: Makes biggest corporations and ultra-wealthy pay their fair share: is paid for by strengthening IRS enforcement against wealthy tax cheats, closing tax loopholes exploited by the wealthiest few, and implementing a 15 percent corporate minimum tax – which applies only to the 150 corporations making earning over $1 billion in profits that pay less than 15% in taxes.

positions.summary: Cosponsored multiple Joint Resolutions of Disapproval to block specific U.S. weapons sales to Israel and wrote to the administration urging it to halt weapons transfers and restrict additional U.S. security assistance to Israel.
positions.quote: I wrote to President Biden and Secretary of State Blinken urging them to halt weapons transfers to Israel following the horrific deaths of seven World Central Kitchen volunteers.

positions.summary: Her official immigration page says she is working to restrict ICE funding and claw back DHS funding approved in H.R. 1, and to limit detention contract length and enforcement at sensitive locations.
positions.quote: I am working with my colleagues to restrict funding for ICE and claw back the funding approved for the DHS in H.R. 1.

positions.summary: In a statement on her vote against a November 2025 funding bill, she backed a discharge petition to extend the ACA tax credits for three years.
positions.quote: It is my sincere hope that, just as we are doing with the petition to release the Epstein files, we can get enough Republicans on board to pass these extensions—and bring much-needed relief to millions of Americans.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture and the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Agriculture-FDA and Interior-Environment subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Served as Ranking Member of the Interior and Environment appropriations subcommittee in the 2023-2024 Congress.

candidates.name: Ronald C. Russell

summary.text: Ronald (Ron) C. Russell is the Republican nominee for Maine's 1st Congressional District and a defense contractor from Kennebunkport. A West Point attendee and Army Special Forces veteran who describes himself as a native Mainer and business owner, he lost to Rep. Chellie Pingree in 2024 and won the 2026 Republican primary for a rematch.

background.text: Grew up on his family's potato farm in northern Maine; describes himself as a native Mainer.
Attended West Point and then served in the U.S. Army as an Airborne Ranger and Special Forces Green Beret; in his words, served 30 years in the military.
After his military service he lived in the South, started a small operations and intelligence business, and worked about 15 years as a Department of Defense contractor.
Returned to Maine to run for office; he is a Kennebunkport resident and had not held elected office before 2024.
Won the 2024 Republican primary over Andrew Piantidosi and lost the November 2024 general election to Pingree by more than 20 points.
Won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary over Joshua James Pietrowicz.

priorities.text: Calls for civility and bipartisan discourse in Congress, saying party-line legislation is often quickly reversed when power changes hands.
priorities.quote: In my view, legislation drawn strictly along party lines wastes time and money, as it is quickly discarded or reversed by executive order when the opposing party takes power.

priorities.text: Prioritizes education reform focused on core subjects (math, science, history, English) and giving parents a stronger voice in schools.

Opposes additional federal taxes on Maine residents, citing the state's already-high state and local tax burden, and supports making the tax relief from the 2025 tax law (the 'Big Beautiful Bill') permanent.
priorities.quote: We need to protect the temporary tax relief gains made by passage of the Big Beautiful Bill and make them permanent.

positions.summary: Campaign website supports background-check integration and mental-health reforms and opposes what he calls burdensome gun-control measures (2024 campaign website).
positions.quote: I support targeted reforms that improve background check integration, expand mental health resources, and strengthen interagency coordination without infringing on constitutional rights.

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for providing law enforcement with resources and paying officers a decent wage to attract recruits (2024 campaign website).
positions.quote: We need to pay our law enforcement and first responders a decent wage so we attract the best and the brightest to the field.

candidates.researchNotes: Priorities come from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; issue statements come from the issue pages of his campaign website (several pages refer to the Biden administration and appear to date from 2024). The site's voter-ID text was not used because it does not address documentary proof of citizenship.

statements.quote: We must prioritize securing our border to stem the illegal flow of unsustainable numbers of immigrants.
statements.context: On his campaign website (page footer shows 2024 copyright; accessed Oct. 19, 2026)

statements.quote: I will not support any efforts to mandate the energy sources that Mainers' choose to power their vehicles or heat their homes.
statements.context: On his campaign website (page footer shows 2024 copyright; accessed Oct. 19, 2026)

statements.quote: We must measure results, reward what works, and embrace reforms like school choice to ensure every student has the best shot at success.
statements.context: On his campaign website (page footer shows 2024 copyright; accessed Oct. 19, 2026)
